title: Introduce local RAG workshop kits and interactive snippet playbook
author: Leah Chen
description: Adds a compact, locally runnable RAG workshop kit and an interactive snippet-driven playbook aimed at onboarding engineers to RAG authoring patterns and telemetry best practices. Motivation: teams repeatedly ask for a small, opinionated workshop that demonstrates retrieval-authoring loops, tool-calling contracts, and lightweight telemetry probes without needing cluster infra. This PR delivers: 1) a quickstarts/rag-workshop kit with a devcontainer and minimal indexer to run a local scenario; 2) an interactive playbook that uses snippet-first examples to teach stepwise troubleshooting and assertions; 3) telemetry probe presets and a small sample dashboard for the Console to highlight token usage and prefix cache hits; 4) example tool-contract stubs and typed bindings for TS/Go to demonstrate safe tool-calling; 5) short tutorial docs and a smoke CI that verifies the devcontainer boots and the local runner completes. Checklist: - [x] author tutorial and README - [x] add devcontainer for reproducible local setup - [x] add small in-memory indexer and sample corpus - [x] instrument telemetry probes and example Console dashboard - [x] include step assertions and snapshots for smoke CI - [x] add example typed contracts for tool-calling - [x] tests and lint passing Local run instructions are included in quickstarts/rag-workshop/README.md. This description includes links to the playbook YAML and snippet index for quick reference. Related: ENG-2145 (onboarding playbooks), PM-327 (workshop roadmap).

release_notes: Added local RAG workshop quickstart with devcontainer, interactive snippet playbook, telemetry probe presets, and typed tool-contract examples. This will help teams onboard faster and validate local RAG flows without cloud infra.
notes_for_maintainers: Keep the sample corpus small to avoid inflating CI artifacts. If adding datasets, place them behind an opt-in fetch script. Telemetry defaults to opt-in in CI and can be disabled via WORKSHOP_TELEMETRY=false in the devcontainer. Consider adding a compact browser-based UI in a follow-up PR.
